title.en: Risk briefing for a mountain trip
title.es: Charla de riesgos para una excursión

es: Presentar en una charla breve los riesgos de una excursión (peligro, probabilidad, consecuencia y medida de prevención) y deducir las causas de un incidente con must have, might have y can't have.

teaching.en: This briefing has three parts: the hazard, the risk and the preventive measure we take, and we will go through them in that order.
teaching.es: Esta charla tiene tres partes: el peligro, el riesgo y la medida preventiva que tomamos, y las repasaremos en ese orden.
teaching.explanationEs: Una charla de riesgos sigue un orden fijo: peligro, riesgo (probabilidad) y medida. Preventive measure = medida para evitar un problema.
segments: This briefing has three parts: the hazard, the risk and the preventive
measure we take, and we will go through them in that order.
teaching.audioText: This briefing has three parts: the hazard, the risk and the preventive measure we take, and we will go through them in that order.

teaching.en: Ice is likely on the ridge, and the consequence could be a serious fall, so participants should treat every step as if it mattered.
teaching.es: Es probable que haya hielo en la cresta y la consecuencia podría ser una caída grave, así que los participantes deberían tratar cada paso como si importara.
teaching.explanationEs: Después de la probabilidad se nombra la consecuencia: could be + lo que podría pasar.
segments: Ice is likely on the ridge, and the consequence could be a
serious fall, so participants should treat every step as if it mattered.
teaching.audioText: Ice is likely on the ridge, and the consequence could be a serious fall, so participants should treat every step as if it mattered.

teaching.en: To prevent a fall, all participants must check their equipment, because a loose strap is often the root cause of an accident.
teaching.es: Para evitar una caída, todos los participantes deben revisar su equipo, porque una correa suelta suele ser la causa de fondo de un accidente.
teaching.explanationEs: To prevent + nombre abre la medida; must marca la obligación. Root cause: la causa de fondo, no el síntoma.
segments: To prevent a fall, all participants must check their equipment, because
a loose strap is often the root cause of an accident.
teaching.audioText: To prevent a fall, all participants must check their equipment, because a loose strap is often the root cause of an accident.

teaching.en: The path was wet after the rain, so the incident must have happened then, and a hiker who slipped could easily sustain an injury.
teaching.es: El camino estaba mojado tras la lluvia, así que el incidente debe de haber ocurrido entonces, y un excursionista que resbalara podría sufrir fácilmente una lesión.
teaching.explanationEs: Must have + participio: deducción casi segura sobre el pasado, a partir de una prueba. Sustain an injury: sufrir una lesión.
segments: The path was wet after the rain, so the incident must have
happened then, and a hiker who slipped could easily sustain an injury.
teaching.audioText: The path was wet after the rain, so the incident must have happened then, and a hiker who slipped could easily sustain an injury.

teaching.en: There is no evidence of wind damage, so the cause can't have been the storm; in hindsight, the late start was the contributing factor.
teaching.es: No hay indicios de daños por el viento, así que la causa no puede haber sido la tormenta; visto en retrospectiva, la salida tardía fue el factor que contribuyó.
teaching.explanationEs: Can't have + participio: deducción negativa casi segura. In hindsight: valorar algo una vez que ya se sabe cómo acabó.
segments: There is no evidence of wind damage, so the cause can't have
been the storm; in hindsight, the late start was the contributing factor.
teaching.audioText: There is no evidence of wind damage, so the cause can't have been the storm; in hindsight, the late start was the contributing factor.

teaching.en: The incident was only a near miss and might have started with a missed turn in the fog, but without more evidence we should treat that as a possibility, not a fact.
teaching.es: El incidente fue solo un casi accidente y podría haber empezado con un giro que no se tomó en la niebla, pero sin más pruebas debemos tratarlo como una posibilidad, no como un hecho.
teaching.explanationEs: Might have + participio: posibilidad sobre el pasado, sin seguridad. Near miss: un percance que pudo acabar mal y no lo hizo.
segments: The incident was only a near miss and might have started with a missed turn in
the fog, but without more evidence we should treat that as a possibility, not a fact.
teaching.audioText: The incident was only a near miss and might have started with a missed turn in the fog, but without more evidence we should treat that as a possibility, not a fact.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Para evitar una caída, los participantes deben revisar su equipo.»

answer.text: To prevent a fall, participants must check their equipment

feedback.es: To prevent + nombre abre la medida; después va el sujeto con must y el verbo base.

hint.es: La frase empieza con To prevent y termina con lo que hay que revisar.

prompt.es: Elige la deducción más segura según la prueba.

choices.text: The hikers must have left a short time ago.
The hikers can't have left a short time ago.
The hikers might have left a long time ago.

feedback.es: Con un fuego aún caliente la prueba es fuerte: must have + participio expresa la deducción casi segura; can't have la descartaría.

hint.es: La prueba es fuerte y reciente: busca must have + participio.

origin.text: The fire is still warm, the tent is empty and the map is gone, but the boots are still by the door.

prompt.es: Completa: «No hay daños por el viento: no puede haber sido la tormenta.»

feedback.es: Can't have + participio deduce que algo pasado es casi imposible; have es parte fija de la estructura.

hint.es: Can't va seguido de have + participio cuando se deduce sobre el pasado.

origin.text: The bridge is safe and the trees are standing. There is no sign of wind damage, so the storm can't ___ been the cause.

prompt.es: Escucha la charla y elige qué medida se toma en el cruce del río.

choices.text: Crossing in pairs to save time and energy.
Crossing one by one, bags held tight.
Sending the bags across first, then the hikers.

feedback.es: La medida contra las caídas en el río es cruzar de uno en uno con las mochilas bien sujetas; el descenso tiene otra medida distinta.

origin.audio: Good morning, and welcome to the briefing. I will cover the hazard, the risk and the preventive measure for each stage. The first hazard is the river crossing. Ice is unlikely today, but fast water could push a hiker off balance, and the consequence could be an injury or lost equipment. To prevent that, we cross one at a time, with every bag held tight to the body. The second hazard is the long descent: tiredness is the root cause of most falls, so we stop for ten minutes every hour and nobody walks at the back alone.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase con su función en la charla.

pairs: The boots are gone, so she must have left.
He might have taken the shorter path.
They can't have reached the summit in an hour.
To prevent a fall, check your equipment.

feedback.es: Must have expresa casi certeza, might have una posibilidad, can't have una imposibilidad casi total y to prevent abre la medida.

pairs: The boots are gone, so she must have left.
He might have taken the shorter path.
They can't have reached the summit in an hour.
To prevent a fall, check your equipment.

prompt.es: Lee el informe: ¿qué concluye sobre la causa del accidente?

choices.text: Poor equipment caused the fall, and preparation was weak.
The wet rock alone explains the whole accident, nothing else.
Tiredness made a fall likely; preparation was sound.

feedback.es: El informe descarta la mala preparación y señala el cansancio como factor que contribuyó a la caída.

origin.text: Incident report, draft: the hiker fell on wet rock at about two o'clock and sustained a minor injury. The path was marked and the group had the right equipment, so the cause can't have been poor preparation. In hindsight, the contributing factor was tiredness: the group had walked for six hours without a proper break.

prompt.es: Escucha el relato: ¿qué dedujo la voluntaria de la estufa fría?

choices.text: That the hikers had left long before.
That somebody was hurt nearby.
That the hikers would be back soon.

feedback.es: Una estufa fría indica que el grupo se fue hace horas: must have left hours earlier.

origin.audio: A mountain volunteer describes a call-out. We found the tent open and the boots gone, she said. The stove was cold, so the people who had been there must have left hours earlier. There was no evidence of a fall or an injury, so it can't have been an accident; more likely the group had decided to move on before the weather changed. In hindsight, we had been worried about nothing.

prompt.es: Escucha otra vez: ¿qué actitud muestra ella al final de su relato?

choices.text: Anger at the hikers for leaving without notice.
Relief, although the alarm led to nothing.
Fear that something serious is still wrong.

feedback.es: «In hindsight, we had been worried about nothing» expresa alivio, aunque la alarma no llevara a nada.

There was no evidence of a fall or an injury, so it can't have been an accident; more likely the group had decided to move on before the weather changed. In hindsight, we had been worried about nothing.

prompt.es: Completa: «El retraso en el puente fue un factor que contribuyó al incidente.»

feedback.es: Contributing factor es el factor que contribuye a un resultado sin ser su causa única.

origin.text: The report names no single person to blame. The late start at the bridge was a contributing ___ in the incident.

prompt.es: Escribe el guion de una charla de riesgos para una excursión.

answer.text: Good morning, everyone. This briefing has three parts: the hazards, the risks and the preventive measures we take. The first hazard is ice on the ridge. It is likely after such a cold night, and the consequence could be a serious injury. To prevent a fall, all participants must check their equipment, and you had better walk slowly. The second hazard is the river. In the unlikely event that the water rises, we will turn back at once. There is a slim chance of thunderstorms after two o'clock, so we will be off the ridge by one. Nobody should cross the river unless the guide says it is safe. Please carry a torch in case we come down after dark. If something goes wrong, we will look for the root cause, not for someone to blame. Are there any questions?
accepted: Good morning, everyone. This briefing has three parts: the hazards, the risks and the preventive measures we take. The first hazard is ice on the ridge. It is likely after such a cold night, and the consequence could be a serious injury. To prevent a fall, all participants must check their equipment, and you had better walk slowly. The second hazard is the river. In the unlikely event that the water rises, we will turn back at once. There is a slim chance of thunderstorms after two o'clock, so we will be off the ridge by one. Nobody should cross the river unless the guide says it is safe. Please carry a torch in case we come down after dark. If something goes wrong, we will look for the root cause, not for someone to blame. Are there any questions?

Hello, team. Today I want to explain two risks. The main hazard is the wind on the high ground. Strong gusts are highly likely, and the consequence could be a fall or another serious injury. To prevent it, we will stay on the marked route, and you had better hold your hats. The other hazard is the cold. The odds are that it will freeze tonight, so everybody must bring a warm coat, provided that there is space in the bag. In case anyone feels dizzy, tell me at once. Unless the forecast improves, we will not climb the summit, and in hindsight that will be the right choice. Does everyone understand the plan?

feedback.es: Una charla clara nombra cada peligro, dice cuán probable es, avisa de la consecuencia y cierra con una medida de prevención y una condición.

origin.text: Vas a dirigir la charla de riesgos de una excursión de un día con una cresta y un río (entre 140 y 200 palabras). Presenta dos peligros con su probabilidad, su consecuencia y una medida de prevención (to prevent, unless, in case, had better).

prompt.es: Escucha: ¿qué postura adopta el guía ante el incidente?

choices.text: He blames the hiker who was hurt.
He denies that anything went wrong.
He wants lessons, not someone to blame.

feedback.es: Pide no culpar a nadie y aprender del incidente: busca lecciones, no culpables.

origin.audio: After the trip, the leader went over what had happened at the bridge. There was no evidence that anyone had ignored the rules, so he said it can't have been a lack of care. The delay might have been caused by the fog, and the injury must have happened when the rock moved under her foot. He asked the group not to blame anyone but to learn from it, because one simple preventive measure would have stopped it: crossing one at a time.

prompt.es: Lee el correo: ¿con qué propósito lo escribe la organización?

choices.text: To justify a new rule without blaming any participant.
To apologise for having cancelled the walk.
To ask participants for evidence about the incident.

feedback.es: Explica una nueva medida tras el incidente y aclara que nadie tuvo la culpa: justifica la norma sin señalar a nadie.

origin.text: Dear participants, thank you for joining last Saturday's walk. Following the incident at the bridge, we have added a preventive measure to every briefing: all groups now cross one at a time. We do not believe anyone was at fault, but in hindsight the old routine was a contributing factor. We hope you will understand why the briefing is now a little longer.

prompt.es: Escribe una frase con so that sobre el equipo y la seguridad.

answer.text: We check the equipment so that nobody gets hurt.
accepted: We check the equipment so that nobody gets hurt.
We check the equipment so that nobody is hurt.
We check the equipment so that no one gets hurt.
We check the equipment so nobody gets hurt.
We always check the equipment so that nobody gets hurt.
We are checking the equipment so that nobody gets hurt.

feedback.es: So that + oración en presente expresa la finalidad de una medida preventiva.

origin.text: Escribe una frase en inglés: revisamos el equipo para que nadie se haga daño.
